newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan bourse closes higher despite thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan bourse closes higher despite thin trade.

text.p: Casablanca stock exchange closed on Wednesday 0.24 percent higher with ONA group and Societe Nationale d'Investissement advancing slightly and a low volume traded on the official market, stockbrokers said.
The bourse all-share index closed at 637.07 points from 635.52 points on Tuesday.
ONA, the biggest Moroccan private conglomerate, gained seven dirhams to 780 dirhams with 1,992 shares exchanged.
SNI, the second largest private group, was up three dirhams to 732 dirhams.
Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur rose eight dirhams to 579 dirhams.
In the energy sector, Samir gained four dirhams to 355 dirhams with 2,895 shares traded.
The mining firm Societe Metallurgique d'Imiter increased by 16 dirhams to 576 dirhams.
First tranche of privatisation bonds, issued in January 1996, fell 11 dirhams to 1,388 dirhams.
Blue-chip Banque Commerciale du Maroc closed unchanged at 860 dirhams while Banque Marocaine pour le Commerce et l'Industrie dropped 31 dirhams to 450 dirhams with 654 shares traded.
Total traded volume on the official market was 12.1 million dirhams from 21 million dirhams.

On the over-the-counter market, the volume was 137.4 from 44.6 million dirhams. Newly-floated credit firm Maghrebail accounted for the main trade in this market with 91,400 shares changing hands, followed by 30,000 ONA shares.
